To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) global sensitivity analysis can be used as a tool to assess identifiability of parameters; 2) global sensitivity analysis allows to identify non-identifiable parameters in the case of correlated sensitivities.

i) global sensitivity analysis is an efficient way of detecting non-identifiabilities in systems of differential equations; ii) global sensitivity measures can be used to assess the correlation between two (or more parameters).

i) the global sensitivity of the model output to model parameters can be used to assess the global identifiability of the model; ii) two correlated sensitivity measures of a model output to two parameters are a sufficient condition to conclude on the global practical non-identification of the parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new tools to handle global sensitivity and identifability problems in systems biology.
the study of the relationships between global sensitivity analysis and global identifiability of parameters.
the study of global sensitivity and identifability measures, and the development of a new method to assess global sensitivity measures in order to derive conditions of non-identifiablity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
global sensitivity and identifibility are closely related.

(i) global sensitivity analysis can provide a first step towards the global identifiability problem; and (ii) global identifiability analysis can help to understand the sensitivity analysis results and to provide more insight on the model.
the practical identifiability of a model can be assessed from the global sensitivity measures of the output of the model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the global sensitivity analysis of the output of a system of differential equations with respect to the model parameters provides useful information to identify the model parameters and to assess their practical identifiability.
global sensitivity measures can be used for practical identifiability assessment of systems biology models.

global sensitivity analysis can be used as a powerful tool in the identifiability analysis of systems biology models, in the sense that it provides a practical way to detect parameters that are not identifiable, and also to find out parameters which are highly correlated, thus reducing the number of parameters to be estimated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sensitivity analysis can provide information on identifiability, especially in large systems of differential equation.
sensitivity measures of the output of a system of differential equations with respect to its parameters are related to the identifiability of these parameters.
global sensitivity and identifibility issues in systems biology can be handled in a unified manner.
